scope: Read-only public upstream metadata for all 68 selected manifests/stack.json components and the current public starred-repository identity delta. This is a dated freshness check, not an exhaustive landscape search, security audit, benchmark, upgrade acceptance, installation, or proof of superiority.

methodology.retries: No unchanged failed API request was retried.
methodology.repository_resolution: GitHub owner/repository extracted from selected repository URL; returned html_url records redirects. Poppler's canonical primary upstream is separately recorded as GitLab, while GitHub checks concern its recorded mirror.
methodology.release_resolution: GitHub /releases/latest resolves the latest non-draft stable release and excludes prereleases. Release tag commits resolved through /commits/{url-encoded-ref}; absent latest endpoints fall back to a default-branch commit solely for source metadata.
methodology.selected_pin_resolution: 40-hex source pins, full-commit versions, and two embedded '@ <40-hex>' versions were resolved. Two archive SHA-256 pins were initially submitted as commit refs; failed attempts are preserved and corrected to archive_digest semantics, without retry.
methodology.output_preservation: Selected public response fields, exact endpoints, exit codes, times and SHA-256 of raw stdout are retained; full response bodies are not bundled. Nonzero stderr is retained in bounded form. No authentication state or token was read or published.
methodology.sanitization: Only public repository metadata, public starred identities and bounded errors are included. Host paths and authentication metadata omitted.
methodology.change_rule: Retain accepted selections until a named capability gap and representative comparison justify an adjustment. Metadata recency alone is insufficient.

summary.recommendation: Retain current qualified pins; review the five newer stable releases against actual capability gaps before upgrading. Refresh canonical Headroom identity in future manifest maintenance without treating its transfer as a functional replacement.

checks.note: The selected source_pin is an archive SHA-256, not a Git commit. This failed interpretation is retained and was not retried.
The selected source_pin is an archive SHA-256, not a Git commit. This failed interpretation is retained and was not retried.

stars.scope: Public user-star endpoint only; no private-star inventory queried. No automatic adoption or code indexing.
stars.identity_hash_format: SHA-256 of newline-joined sorted lowercase repository URLs; no final newline.
stars.repository_snapshot_method: Seven explicit 50-item pages queried after the initial paginated identity-delta check so the complete public identity list is retained. The seven-page list must reproduce the initial 343-identity set hash.

added_reviews.role: Native desktop computer-use driver, optional VM/cloud desktop infrastructure and evaluation tooling
added_reviews.license_scope: Root LICENSE.md inspected in full; model/dataset artifacts and external runtime dependencies may have separate terms and were not audited.
added_reviews.rationale: Retain as a conditional complement for native desktop tasks that require application interaction beyond browser DOM automation. Pinned upstream docs describe Driver MCP/CLI and SDK integration, cloud desktop fleets, Apple-Silicon Lume VMs, and benchmarks. The first-app tutorial explicitly covers macOS, Windows and Linux, so platform incompatibility is not a supported blanket rejection. Existing agent-browser/native UI defaults remain selected because this review did not demonstrate a failed task they solve poorly or a same-task Cua advantage; source claims and a Calculator tutorial alone do not establish performance or deployment readiness.

comparison.retained_selected_role: Qualified browser snapshot/ref interaction plus the host's supported native UI tools.
comparison.distinct_candidate_fit: Cross-application native desktop actions and optional isolated desktop infrastructure.
comparison.why_not_default: No installed or executed Cua task, recovery test, latency/cost comparison, permission-lifecycle check or new-host reproduction is retained for this candidate.
comparison.overturn_with: Run the upstream first-app example and a representative multi-application task on the target OS, compare completion/correctness, focus behavior, permission attribution, recovery and operational cost against existing tools. Adopt only the component that closes the demonstrated task gap.

findings: Root README presents a modular computer-use stack; its components are not an instruction to adopt cloud hosting or model weights.
Driver README documents MCP over stdio and CLI use by existing agents, with separate Python/TypeScript application SDKs.
The first-app tutorial's declared outcome is Calculator 6 x 7 = 42 across macOS, Windows and Linux. Its visible macOS setup requires Accessibility and Screen Recording grants.
Lume in the root README specifically targets local macOS/Linux VMs on Apple Silicon; this limitation cannot be generalized to Cua Driver.
Driver macOS process identity documentation requires responsible app attribution and supported launch modes; this operational boundary was inspected, not exercised.

reviewed_files.extent: Purpose, component, Fleet, Lume, CUA-S1 and benchmark sections.
Integration surfaces, architecture/test pointers and macOS identity/permission sections.

limitations: Source/documentation review only; no installation, desktop action, cloud resource creation, model inference or upstream test ran.
No claim that Cua failed a fair comparison or is inferior overall; it remains an unqualified targeted candidate.
The initial guessed root LICENSE path returned HTTP 404; root listing located LICENSE.md, which was read successfully. The failed path query is preserved.
Root README and Driver README exceed the output bound; selected indexed source sections were inspected rather than every source file.
The tutorial excerpt is limited to its first 85 lines and 3700 characters; Windows/Linux setup details and the full test suite were not independently validated.

limits: Freshness metadata is not evidence that a selected repository is the best in its field, nor that another candidate failed a behavioral comparison.
No upstream tests, installations, model inference, broker operations, release-body feature/security review or whole-ecosystem new-host acceptance were performed in this snapshot.
Five GitHub latest-stable endpoints returned 404; this does not imply abandoned software, absent tags/packages, or an unavailable primary non-GitHub release channel.
Selected archive SHA-256 values are retained from the manifest and were not re-downloaded or rehashed; resolving a Git commit or release does not verify installed bytes.
Default branches and release tags are mutable; retained source SHAs and query timestamps bound this observation.

Public stars are discovery preferences, not a quality ranking. The one added repository received a bounded primary-source screen and remains a conditional targeted candidate; it was not installed or adopted.
Full upstream API bodies are not retained, so output hashes identify the observed bodies but cannot reconstruct them.
